questions.text: How much does an individual membership cost per year?

evidenceUnits.quote: An individual membership costs 40 dollars per year.

questions.text: What is the late fee per tool for each overdue day?

evidenceUnits.quote: The library charges a late fee of 1 dollar per tool for each day the tool is overdue.

questions.text: How long does a safety checkout take?

evidenceUnits.quote: A safety checkout takes about 45 minutes and is free for members.

questions.text: How far in advance do workshop bench reservations open?

evidenceUnits.quote: Reservations open fourteen days in advance and are made through the member portal.

questions.text: When is the returns drop box at the loading dock open?

evidenceUnits.quote: The returns drop box at the loading dock is open at all times except during snow removal.

questions.text: How many items can each clinic visitor bring?

evidenceUnits.quote: Clinic visitors may bring up to two items each.

questions.text: Are yearly dues waived for people on county aid?

evidenceUnits.quote: Members who receive county food or housing assistance may join for free; no proof beyond the assistance card is required.

questions.text: If somebody is waiting for the drill I have, may I keep it another week?

evidenceUnits.quote: A loan can be renewed once, online or at the desk, if no other member has placed a hold on that tool.

questions.text: What happens if I hang on to something for more than a month?

evidenceUnits.quote: A tool that is more than 30 days overdue is treated as lost.

questions.text: Will I be billed because my saw got blunt from ordinary use?

evidenceUnits.quote: Normal wear, such as dull blades or worn sanding pads, is never charged to the member.

questions.text: May I use an aerosol finish on my furniture indoors?

evidenceUnits.quote: Finishing work with spray paint, lacquer or other solvent-based products is not allowed indoors because the room does not have a spray booth.

questions.text: Who keeps the equipment in good working order?

evidenceUnits.quote: It has two paid staff members: a coordinator who manages volunteers and the catalog, and a part-time technician who maintains and repairs the tools.

questions.text: How can I earn a membership without paying by helping out?

evidenceUnits.quote: Volunteers who give at least 24 hours in a calendar year receive a free individual membership for the following year.

questions.text: What should I wear to the saw training?

evidenceUnits.quote: Members must bring closed-toe shoes and must tie back long hair before the session begins.

questions.text: Is the library ever open on a Sunday?

evidenceUnits.quote: The library is closed on Sunday and Monday.
The repair clinic meets on the third Sunday of each month in the workshop, from noon to 3:00 p.m.

questions.text: How many tools can a household have out, and how does a pressure washer count?

evidenceUnits.quote: A household membership shares a limit of eight tools across all of its cards.
Large items, such as tile saws, pressure washers and the trailer-mounted wood chipper, count as two tools each.

questions.text: What is the most I could owe in late fees on one tool, and when do unpaid fees block new checkouts?

evidenceUnits.quote: Late fees stop growing after 20 dollars per tool.
Members with more than 10 dollars in unpaid fees cannot check out new tools until the balance is paid.

questions.text: What do I need to borrow the wood chipper, and how often can I take it?

evidenceUnits.quote: The wood chipper can only be borrowed by members who bring a vehicle with a rated towing hitch.
Loans of the chipper are limited to one weekend per member per month.
